title: Heterogeneous mixture-of-experts for long-horizon vessel trajectory prediction across regional datasets
content:
by Yuxiang Tan, Yingqiang Cai, Kuan Fan, Xiaowen Li, Guangyu Qiu

Long-horizon vessel trajectory prediction for maritime traffic monitoring and route planning requires both a prompt response to manoeuvres and control of error accumulation. UnifiedInternalMoE combines a motion-prior residual expert with four temporal predictors in a separate checkpoint for each region and seed. Convex weights are fitted to validation predictions at 5, 10, and 60 min and interpolated to produce the complete future trajectory. A ten-seed comparison across four regions, together with capacity controls, learned gating, and internal ablations, evaluates the benefit of the heterogeneous combination and its sources. In a five-seed evaluation on an independent Finnish AIS subset, the fusion has the lowest mean average displacement error (ADE) at all six horizons, with ADE@60 of 1719.53±25.80 m; it does not consistently lead in long-horizon final displacement error (FDE) or frozen source-to-target transfer. These results support the applicability of the same architecture when retrained for different regions and its use as a forecasting reference for shore-based analysis of long-horizon motion trends. Its applicability remains limited by the number of independent vessels, regional distribution differences, and computational cost.
